gen-dafont-capture-it-fs-bespoke-serif: A towering x-height gives Capture It its urban muscle, with letters so tightly shut they look nearly sealed. Bespoke Serif follows as a classic serif, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones; try the heading much larger than the text.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-archivo: Retro and boxy, Commodore 64 sets fixed-width, code-style letters with a hint of modulation you only catch up close. Archivo takes over as a plain sans with outward-opening curves and a tall x-height, giving the typewriter-ish heading a friendly editorial partner.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-fs-amulya: Amulya reads modern and generous, its curves leaving wide gaps that let each word breathe. Commodore 64 is best at tight, shuttered, code-style headings, while Amulya is best at carrying open, easygoing sans-serif text.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-fs-be-vietnam-pr: Fixed-width, code-style letters with a snug, shuttered lowercase make Commodore 64 feel like an old terminal that has been polished up. Be Vietnam Pro does the open, even-lined text work, while the heading keeps the nostalgia.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-fs-chillax: Chillax reads loose and casual, its lines looping like spaghetti with curves that never quite close. Commodore 64 brings the shuttered, fixed-width, code-style punch up top, so make the Chillax text a touch larger and its relaxed shapes stay easy to follow.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-fs-merriweather-: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, with tall lowercase and an e that opens clearly. Commodore 64 does best with its snug, closed, fixed-width letters at display size, while Merriweather Sans is the one built to carry the text.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-plus-jakarta-san: Nostalgic and a bit boxy, Commodore 64 brings fixed-width, code-style letters whose stroke weight shifts noticeably without ever turning dramatic. And Plus Jakarta Sans does the precise, monoline text work, keeping its curve endings well apart.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-work-sans: Commodore 64 brings classic, nostalgic, fixed-width letters with a snug, shuttered lowercase and only a moderate height. Work Sans, with its high mean line, is the sharper, taller counterweight.
gen-dafont-eraser-poppins: Eraser comes in bold and understated, every stroke the same weight with no thick or thin parts. And Poppins brings the sturdy, tall lowercase and loose, open curves of a plain sans, which is the pair's real strength.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-sentient: Industrial and modern, Existence opens its lowercase like wide glass portholes. Sentient answers in a pinched, closed-in serif with crossbars a touch thinner than the stems, and that sophisticated hush is the pair's strongest quality.
